title: The interview question
summary: Clara prepares answers for every possible interview question except the one she is actually asked.
paragraphs: Clara had prepared for the interview for a whole week. She had researched the company, a small travel agency that organised walking holidays. She had practised answers in front of the mirror: her strengths, her weaknesses, why she wanted the job, where she saw herself in five years. She had even written notes on small cards, which she now held in her pocket like a lucky {{charm}}.

The interview was with the owner, a tall man called Mr Varela, in an office full of maps and walking boots. He asked her a few normal questions, and Clara answered well. Then he leaned back in his chair. "Tell me," he said, "about a time you got completely lost."

Clara {{froze}}. This wasn't on any of her cards. For a moment she thought about inventing something impressive. Then she remembered a real story. When she was nineteen, she went walking in the Pyrenees with a friend. They took a wrong path, the fog came down, and they spent three hours walking in circles before they found a farmhouse. The farmer's wife gave them soup and told them the way down.

She told the story honestly, including the parts that made her look silly, like the fact that she had a map in her bag the whole time and forgot about it. Mr Varela laughed. Then he asked, "What did you learn?" Clara thought. "To stay calm," she said. "To ask for help. And to check my bag before I {{panic}}."

She got the job. On her first day, Mr Varela explained. "Everyone prepares perfect answers," he said. "But in this business, things go wrong: buses don't come, rivers flood, people get lost. I need someone who can tell me what really happened and what they did next." Clara still keeps her interview cards in a drawer. She has never needed them. She tells the farmhouse story to every group she {{guides}}.

charm.meaning: a small object that people believe brings good luck

froze.meaning: suddenly stopped moving or thinking because of fear or surprise

panic.meaning: suddenly feel so afraid that you cannot think clearly

guides.meaning: shows people the way, especially on a tour

questions.question: How had Clara prepared for the interview?
options: She asked a friend to interview her.
She researched the company and practised answers in front of a mirror.
She went walking in the mountains.
She wrote a long letter to Mr Varela.
questions.explanation: She researched the company and practised answers in front of the mirror.

questions.question: Why did Clara freeze?
options: Mr Varela was rude to her.
The question was not one she had prepared for.
questions.explanation: The question about getting lost wasn't on any of her cards.

questions.question: Which part of her story made her look silly?
options: She had a map in her bag and forgot about it.
questions.explanation: She had a map in her bag the whole time and forgot about it.

questions.question: Why did Mr Varela like her answer?
options: It was the most impressive story he had heard.
He needs someone who is honest about problems and what they did next.
She had worked in a travel agency before.
questions.explanation: He needs someone who can tell him what really happened and what they did next.
